The department values hands-on, experiential education and prepares students for professional success in nutrition, dietetics, and food science. Offering specializations in Dietetics, Nutrition Science, Nutrition and Health, and Food Science and Technology, it blends classroom instruction with lab-based research and culinary innovation. Faculty engage in applied scholarship spanning community nutrition, food safety, and plant-based foods, and the department maintains rigorous accreditation standards from ACEND, IFT, and the Research Chefs Association-reflecting its commitment to industry relevance and academic excellence. Students benefit from state-of-the-art teaching kitchens, sensory evaluation labs, pilot-scale processing facilities, and nutrition counseling spaces. Engagement extends beyond the classroom through student organizations like the Foods & Nutrition Forum, Food Science Society (IFTSA), and honor societies (Phi Upsilon Omicron, Phi Tau Sigma). Co-curricular programs include internships with hospitals, government agencies, and food companies, plus study-abroad and Spanish-language Dietetics tracks. courses.title: Orientation and Careers in Food Science and Technology
courses.description: Orientation and discussion of academic expectations and procedures for students in the Food Science and Technology major. Introduction to careers, professional associations and publications in the field of Food Science and Technology.
courses.prerequisites: FST Major.

courses.title: Introduction to Food Science and Technology
courses.description: An introduction to the scope, principles and practices of food science and technology. Basic aspects of chemistry, microbiology and sensory analysis of food products. Introduction to food packaging, safety and sanitation and basics of food laws and regulations. Principles of food engineering and the most common methods of food preservation. Overview on sustainability and the commercial processing of specific food commodities.

courses.title: Design and Analysis for Food Science
courses.description: Introduction and application of quantitative design and data analysis relevant to food science subject areas. The application of quantitative reasoning and statistical methods for data analysis and experimental design in R&D process involving specific commodity-based product and process development. The basics of technical writing and reporting relevant to food science research and industrial practices. Development of evidence-based technical communication skills necessary for upper division food science and technology technical courses. Corequisite(s): FST 2250A . Pre or Corequisite(s): C- or better in FST 1250 ; and C- or better in STA 1200 , STA 1202 , or STA 1300 .

courses.description: Introduction and application of quantitative design and data analysis relevant to food science subject areas. courses.title: Science of Food and Cooking
courses.description: Introduction to the basic building blocks in food and their applications in the culinary art. Emphasis on understanding how various food preparation methods impact food texture and flavor. Application of experimental design to optimize the food properties.

courses.title: Sensory Evaluation of Foods
courses.description: Principles, theory and methodology of sensory evaluation of foods and applications in consumer testing and food research and development. Corequisite(s): FST 3180L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in FST 2250 and FST 2250A , or FST 1250 or FST 125 in curriculum year 20-21 and prior.

courses.title: Sensory Evaluation of Foods Laboratory
courses.description: Principles, theory and methodology of sensory evaluation of foods and applications in consumer testing and food research and development. Corequisite(s): FST 3180 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in FST 2250 and FST 2250A , or FST 1250 or FST 125 in curriculum year 20-21 and prior.

courses.title: Food Packaging
courses.description: Exploration of the role of food packaging in food preservation. Discussion of food packaging materials and their impact on food products. Overview of product stability and shelf life extension. Demonstrations and design activities. Corequisite(s): FST 3190A (not required for Culinology Option students).
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 2010 or CHM 201; CHM 2010L or CHM 250L; PHY 1210 or PHY 121; PHY 1210L or PHY 121L; and FST 2250 and FST 2250A , or FST 1250 or FST 125 in curriculum year 20-21 and prior.

courses.title: Food Packaging Activity
courses.description: Exploration of the role of food packaging in food preservation. Discussion of food packaging materials and their impact on food products. Overview of product stability and shelf life extension. Demonstrations and design activities. Corequisite(s): FST 3190 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 2010 or CHM 201; CHM 2010L or CHM 250L; PHY 1210 or PHY 121; PHY 1210L or PHY 121L; and FST 2250 and FST 2250A , or FST 1250 or FST 125 in curriculum year 20-21 and prior.

courses.title: Experimental Food Science
courses.description: Experimental study of ingredient functions and factors affecting food product quality as measured by sensory and objective methods. Guided group projects involving problem identification, literature search, project design, data collection, and critical analysis of data, oral and written presentations of findings. 2 hours lecture/problem solving. Corequisite(s): FST 3210L .
courses.prerequisites: NTR major and C- or better in the following: NTR 1210 ; NTR 1210L ; CHM 2010 or CHM 3150 ; and NTR 3130W .

courses.title: Experimental Food Science Laboratory
courses.description: Experimental study of ingredient functions and factors affecting food product quality as measured by sensory and objective methods. Guided group projects involving problem identification, literature search, project design, data collection, and critical analysis of data, oral and written presentations of findings. 1 three-hour laboratory. Corequisite(s): FST 3210 .
courses.prerequisites: NTR major and C- or better in the following: NTR 1210 ; NTR 1210L ; CHM 2010 or CHM 3150 ; NTR 3130W ; and STA 1200 or STA 1202 .

courses.title: Food Laws and Regulations
courses.description: An examination of the rules and regulations of various governmental agencies with regard to the processing, packaging, labeling and marketing of food products. Sources of information necessary for communication with government on public food policy information.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in FST 1250 , ABM 2010 , or NTR 1210 ; and C- or better in ENG 2105 or PHL 2020 .

courses.title: Food Safety and Current Issues
courses.description: [GE 5D] Overview of physical, chemical and microbiological hazards and their role in foodborne illness and the safety of the food supply. Introduction to the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point System. The role of government and basic aspects of food safety laws and regulations. Review of current issues in food safety, food protection, food production, and food processing as they relate to public health.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Food Process Engineering
courses.description: Process engineering principles and related calculations are introduced for food processing applications, including unit conversion, thermodynamics, material and energy balance, basic fluid mechanics, steady-state and unsteady-state heat transfer, psychrometry, and refrigeration. Corequisite(s): FST 3321L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 1220 or CHM 123; CHM 1220L or CHM 123L; PHY 1210 or PHY 121; PHY 1210L or PHY 121L; MAT 1200 or MAT 120; and FST 2250 and FST 2250A , or FST 1250 or FST 125 in curriculum year 20-21 and prior.

courses.title: Food Process Engineering Laboratory
courses.description: Process engineering principles and related calculations are introduced for food processing applications, including unit conversion, thermodynamics, material and energy balance, basic fluid mechanics, steady-state and unsteady-state heat transfer, psychrometry, and refrigeration. Corequisite(s): FST 3321 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 1220 or CHM 123; CHM 1220L or CHM 123L; PHY 1210 or PHY 121; PHY 1210L * or PHY 121L; MAT 1200 or MAT 120; and FST 2250 and FST 2250A , or FST 1250 or FST 125 in curriculum year 20-21 and prior.

courses.title: Introduction to Plant Based Functional Foods
courses.description: An introduction to functional foods and associated laws and regulations. Classification and chemistry of nutraceuticals and bioactive components in plant based functional foods and their health benefits. Factors involved in the development of new plant based functional foods.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 2030 , NTR 2050 , NTR 2350 , or NTR 3050 .

courses.title: Effect of Processing on Plant Based Foods
courses.description: An introduction to different processing techniques such as thermal, nonthermal and others used by food industry to process food on large scale. Effect of processing on bioactive components. Use of processing techniques to produce new functional foods and protect bioactive components.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 2030 , NTR 2050 , NTR 2350 , or NTR 3050 .

courses.title: Food Microbiology
courses.description: Cross Listed as: BIO 3640 A study of the roles of microorganisms in food spoilage, foodborne illness, and fermentation. Factors that influence microbial growth in food and how the growth can be controlled are discussed.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L .

courses.title: Food Science Colloquium
courses.description: Interaction of students with professionals in Food Science and Technology, with emphasis on technical, regulatory, and industry trends. Presenters also share information on their background and careers in the food and beverage industries, public agencies or other organizations. Resume and job interview preparation. Networking practices.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: ENG 2105 or ENG 130; FST 2250 and FST 2250A , or FST 1250 or FST 125 in curriculum year 20-21 and prior; FST 3250 or FST 325; CHM 3150 , CHM 2010 , CHM 201, or CHM 316; CHM 1220 or CHM 123; PHY 1210 or PHY 121; PHY 1210L or PHY 121L; MAT 1200 , MAT 1150 , MAT 120, or MAT 115; BIO 2060 or MIC 201; and BIO 2060L or MIC 201L.

courses.title: Unit Operations in Food Processing
courses.description: An in-depth understanding of food processing technologies, including traditional and emerging methods. Explore the principles, equipment, and applications of various processing techniques such as dehydration, microwave processing, high-pressure processing, spray drying, extrusion, sous vide, and membrane filtration.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: CHM 2010 , CHM 201, CHM 3150 , or CHM 316; CHM 2010L , CHM 250L, CHM 3150L , or CHM 317L; FST 3321 or FST 332; FST 3321L or FST 332L; BIO 2060 or MIC 201; and BIO 2060L or MIC 201L.

courses.title: Food Systems in Nations Abroad II
courses.description: Direct field observation and academic study of food systems in country(s) abroad. Site visits may include government, academia, production, processing, packaging facilities and cultural sights. Includes a field trip to a nation(s) abroad during one of the university recesses. International program costs apply to cover the faculty-led study abroad or field trip. Airfare and tuition are not included in the program cost.
courses.prerequisites: Nutrition or Food Science majors or minors, and FST 4240 , or instructor consent.

courses.title: Food Chemistry
courses.description: Chemical, physical and functional properties of major and minor food components. Major components include water, carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and minor components include pigments, enzymes, vitamins, minerals and food additives. Chemical changes occurring to food components during processing and storage of foods. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): FST 4261LW .
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing, and C- or better in the following: FST 2250 / FST 2250A , CHM 2010 or CHM 3150 , and CHM 2010L or CHM 3150L .

courses.title: Unit Operations in Food Processing II
courses.description: Study of mechanical separations, separation and concentration using membranes, dehydration, evaporation, packaging and other unit operations in food processing that involve mass transfer with or without heat transfer. 2 hours lecture/discussion. Corequisite(s): FST 4271L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in FST 4170 or FST 417.

courses.title: Unit Operations in Food Processing Laboratory
courses.description: Study of unit operations used in food processing technology through hands on laboratory experiments, demonstrations and/or field trips on topics covered in FST 4170 and FST 4271 including raw materials preparation, size reduction, homogenization, pasteurization, canning, mechanical separations, dehydration, etc. Pre or Corequisite(s): C- or better in FST 4170 or FST 417.

courses.title: Food Analysis
courses.description: Principles, methods, and techniques of qualitative and quantitative physical, chemical, and biological analyses of food and food ingredients. Corequisite(s): FST 4280L .
courses.prerequisites: C or better in FST 4261W or FST 421 and FST 4261LW or FST 420L.

courses.title: Food Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: Principles, methods, and techniques of qualitative and quantitative physical, chemical, and biological analyses of food and food ingredients. Corequisite(s): FST 4280 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in FST 4261W or FST 420 and FST 4261LW or FST 420L.

courses.title: Food Product Development
courses.description: Application of food science and technology principles to food research and development industrial practices. Corequisite(s): FST 4290L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: FST 3180 or FST 318, FST 3220 or FST 322, FST 3250 or FST 325, FST 3321 or FST 332, BIO 2060 or MIC 201, BIO 2060L or MIC 201L, CHM 2010 or CHM 201, and CHM 2010L or CHM 250L.

courses.description: Application of food science and technology principles to food research and development industrial practices. Corequisite(s): FST 4290 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: FST 3180 or FST 318, FST 3220 or FST 322, FST 3250 or FST 325, FST 3321 or FST 332, BIO 2060 or MIC 201, BIO 2060L or MIC 201L, CHM 2010 or CHM 201, and CHM 2010L or CHM 250L.

courses.title: Principles of Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point and Other Food Safety Management Systems
courses.description: Basic principles and application of the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) system in food and beverage manufacturing. Regulatory aspects, pre-requisite programs, and preliminary steps for plan design and implementation are also covered. Other food safety management systems, including Preventive Controls for Human Food will also be introduced. Corequisite(s): FST 4300A .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: BIO 3640 , FST 3640 , or MIC 201; BIO 3640L or MIC 201L; FST 3220 or FST 322; FST 3250 or FST 325; and FST 4170 or FST 417.

courses.description: Basic principles and application of the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) system in food and beverage manufacturing. Regulatory aspects, pre-requisite programs, and preliminary steps for plan design and implementation are also covered. Other food safety management systems, including Preventive Controls for Human Food will also be introduced. Corequisite(s): FST 4300 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: BIO 3640 , FST 3640 , or MIC 201; BIO 3640L or MIC 201L; FST 3220 or FST 322; FST 3250 or FST 325; and FST 4170 or FST 417.

courses.description: Cross Listed as: On-the-job training in the professional field of food science and technology. Potential experiences include: quality control and assurance, food safety assurance, industrial production, research and development, product development, sensory testing, inspections/audits, and regulatory activities.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in FST 3900 or FST 390.

Regular meetings and discussions with the advisor are required. Credit is assigned upon acceptance and approval of a completed project.

courses.prerequisites: Advancement to Candidacy required ( NTR 6930 ), graduate standing, and consent of instructor required. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 6940 .

courses.title: Comprehensive Exam
courses.description: Comprehensive exams assess student ability to integrate the knowledge of the area, show critical and independent thinking, and demonstrate a mastery of the subject matter. The assessments consist of three elements: 1) critical analysis presentation; 2) written exams; and 3) oral defense.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation

courses.description: Orientation to the College of Agriculture, careers in Nutrition Science, Food Service and Dietetics. Introduction to professional associations, publications and legislation pertinent to the professions discussed. Required of all Dietetics and Nutrition Science students.Â
courses.prerequisites: Nutrition majors or minors.

courses.description: Application and theory of food science concepts such as food composition, functional properties, and structure of foods. Study of food categories and basic culinary techniques. This course is required for: Dietetic majors, nutrition minors, and as an elective for Food Science majors. This course is required for: Dietetic majors, nutrition minors, and as an elective for Food Science majors. Corequisite(s): NTR 1210L .

courses.title: Health, Nutrition and the Integrated Being
courses.description: Investigation of specific areas of the integrated being dealing with nutrition, stress, drugs, sexuality, major health problems and death and dying. The integrated being and the development of behaviors and actions that will promote optimum physical and mental health will be investigated.

courses.title: Personal and Consumer Nutrition
courses.description: Improve knowledge and understanding of nutrition, nutrients, fitness and food safety related to health and wellness. Make healthy food choices based on MyPlate and other health recommendations. Consumer-decision making skills in meal planning, diet and exercise to aid in better diet, health and wellness.

courses.title: Ethnic Studies of Food, Nutrition, and Health Disparities
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 2180 Interdisciplinary study of Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latina and Latino American communities and food, nutrition, and health inequities in the United States. Foundational theoretical concepts of ethnic studies and nutrition such as racism, colonialism, immigration, eurocentrism, social determinants of health, food and health disparities, acculturation, and health equity are examined.

courses.title: Ethnic Studies of Food, Nutrition, and Health Disparities Service Learning
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 2180 Interdisciplinary study of Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latina and Latino American communities and food, nutrition, and health inequities in the United States. Foundational theoretical concepts of ethnic studies and nutrition such as racism, colonialism, immigration, eurocentrism, social determinants of health, food and health disparities, acculturation, and health equity are examined.

courses.title: Nutrition
courses.description: For nutrition, dietetics, food science and technology majors, healthcare majors and physiology minors. Study of individual nutrient requirements. Utilization of dietary guidelines and other nutrition recommendations. Digestion, absorption, metabolism and excretion of macronutrients and micronutrients. Role of nutrition in health promotion, disease prevention and treatment of disease.
courses.prerequisites: Nutrition Major, Food Science and Technology Major, Nutrition Minor, or Physiology Minor.

courses.title: Nutrition Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory to learn and utilize ESHA Food Processor software. Data interpretation of nutrient analysis required for the nutrition profession and in the following classes: NTR 2350, NTR 3280/L, FST 3210/L, NTR 4430/L.
courses.prerequisites: Nutrition majors and minors only. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 2350 .

courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Nutrition, Science and Health
courses.description: [GE 5D] Integrative approach to nutrition, health, and fitness based on physiological and biochemical principles. Role of diet and other influences in promoting wellness and preventing degenerative diseases. Nutritional self-assessment project/weekly assignments/current controversies, submitted online typed discussions/assignments.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Introduction to Nutrition Research
courses.description: Introduction to nutrition research as the foundation for evidence-based practice. The scientific method, hypothesis testing, clinical trials, epidemiological research, and nutrition surveys. Reading research journal articles and writing a literature review paper. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: C or better STA 1200 or STA 1202 , C- or better in NTR 2350 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Food and Culture
courses.description: [GE 4C] Interrelationship of food availability, historical developments, socio-economic institutions, political, religious, and other influences on food patterns. In-depth study of a selected culture.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Food and Culture Laboratory
courses.description: Selected cultures, religious, traditional, medically modified cultural specialties, therapeutic modifications, countries and hands-on regional food preparation. Meal management according to culture preferences, and nutrient analysis software. Also, exploration of diverse worldviews as pertains relationships between food, history, culture and traditions. Individual oral reports and group projects.
courses.prerequisites: Nutrition Major, NTR 1210 or FN 121, and NTR 1210L or FN 121L. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 2280 or NTR 3280 .

courses.title: Nutrition of the Life Cycle
courses.description: Nutritional needs of all lifecycle stages: pregnancy, lactation, infancy, toddler, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and elderly. Planning and computation of normal diets for all phases of the life cycle. Reading and reporting of current developments in nutrition.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in the following: NTR 2350 or FN 235, NTR 2350L or FN 235L, BIO 2350 or BIO 235, and BIO 2350L or BIO 235L.

courses.title: Nutrition and Life Cycle Applications in Spanish Activity
courses.description: Study of key nutrition terminology in Spanish as related to physiology, individual nutrient needs across the life cycle and the development and prevention of chronic diseases among the Hispanic/Latino population. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 3350 ; and SPN 2111 , SPN 251, or Spanish Placement Exam score of 400+.

courses.title: Nutrition Education and Counseling
courses.description: Principles of learning, evaluation and counseling applied to nutrition. Development of instructional systems including objectives, learning activities and strategies in various settings. Identification and analysis of current problems inherent in such applications. Discussion of interviewing techniques, assessment tools, ethics, outcome measures, documentation and reimbursement. Corequisite(s): NTR 3450A or NTR 3450AS.
courses.prerequisites: B- or better in NTR 3050 or NTR 2350 . Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 3350 .

courses.title: Nutrition Education and Counseling Activity
courses.description: Application of nutrition education and counseling theories and practices including role-playing, interviewing techniques and counseling sessions. Selection, implementation and evaluation of nutrition education materials and programs. Corequisite(s): NTR 3450 .
courses.prerequisites: B- or better in NTR 3050 or NTR 2350 . Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 3350 .

courses.title: Vegetarian and Plant Based Diets
courses.description: Applications, research, theories, and health benefits of vegetarian and plant-based diets (PBDs). Includes discussion on food composition, benefits of PBDs, nutrition composition food categories and color. Diet modifications and alternatives to animal-based products are discussed. *The enforcement of this corequisite has been temporarily suspended in response to the switch to virtual and remote modes of instruction. Corequisite(s): NTR 3580L *.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 2030 , NTR 2050 , NTR 2350 / NTR 2350L , or NTR 3050 .

courses.title: Plant Based Meal Planning
courses.description: Cooking and processing of plant-based produce. Focus on menu development and meal planning for a plant based diet. Attention to nutrition, variety, and palatability will be reviewed for each menu. This course is designed to complement the material covered in the NTR 3580 . Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 3580 / NTR 3580L .

courses.title: Vegetarian and Plant Based Diets Lab
courses.description: Cooking and processing of plant-based produce. Focus on cooking techniques that enhance flavor, palatability, texture, and nutrition. This course is designed to complement the material covered in the NTR 3580 lecture. *The enforcement of this corequisite has been temporarily suspended in response to the switch to virtual and remote modes of instruction. Corequisite(s): NTR 3580 *.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 2030 , NTR 2050 , NTR 2350 / NTR 2350L , or NTR 3050 .

courses.title: Institutional Food Service I
courses.description: Introduction to foodservice management through a systems approach perspective. Production planning, quantity food production. Principles and practices in planning, preparing and serving food. Beginning of facility planning project, including marketing, business plans, goals and objectives. Course includes ServSafe Certification. Laboratory applies principles learned in lecture. Corequisite(s): NTR 3670L .
courses.prerequisites: NTR 1210 or FN 121, and NTR 1210L or FN 121L.

courses.title: Institutional Food Service I Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to foodservice management through a systems approach perspective. Production planning, quantity food production. Principles and practices in planning, preparing and serving food. Beginning of facility planning project, including marketing, business plans, goals and objectives. Course includes ServSafe Certification. Laboratory applies principles learned in lecture. Corequisite(s): NTR 3670 .
courses.prerequisites: NTR 1210 or FN 121, and NTR 1210L or FN 121L.

courses.title: Institutional Food Service II
courses.description: Management of foodservice facilities using menu as a basis for determining recipes, specifications, receiving and storage standards. Purchasing for the foodservice industry. Continuation of facility planning project. Corequisite(s): NTR 3680L .
courses.prerequisites: NTR 3670 or FN 357, and NTR 3670L or FN 357L.

courses.title: Institutional Food Service II Laboratory
courses.description: Management of foodservice facilities using menu as a basis for determining recipes, specifications, receiving and storage standards. Purchasing for the foodservice industry. Continuation of facility planning project. Laboratory applies principles learned in lecture. Corequisite(s): NTR 3680 .
courses.prerequisites: NTR 3670 or FN 357, and NTR 3670L or FN 357L.

courses.title: Farm-to-Table
courses.description: Cross Listed as: PLT 3860 Study of the farm-to-table movement. Focus in this course will be on small scale production, farmer’s markets and utilization of farm products. For nutrition, plant science, hospitality, and food science majors as well as plant-based nutrition and urban agriculture minors.

courses.title: Advanced Nutrient Metabolism I
courses.description: Macronutrients and their metabolism with an emphasis on regulation, structure, digestion, absorption, transport, distribution, and disease states. Integration and regulation of metabolism. Hormonal effects. Written analysis of metabolism and current research.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in NTR 3130W or FN 263, and C or better in NTR 3350 or FN 335. Pre or Corequisite(s): CHM 3210 .

courses.title: Advanced Nutrient Metabolism II
courses.description: Vitamins and minerals as regulatory nutrients. Sources, absorption, transport and storage. Functions and mechanisms of action. Interactions with other nutrients. Metabolism and excretion. Dietary reference intakes and recommended dietary allowances. Written analysis, diagramming metabolic pathways, and critique of current research.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in NTR 3930 or FN 433.

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Nutrition, Inflammation, and Chronic Diseases
courses.description: Study of the inflammatory process and the effects of nutrition on prevention of and pathophysiology of selected chronic diseases; and nutritional quackery. Cannot be substituted for NTR 4430/4430A/4440. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 3350 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Food Service Administration
courses.description: Management principles in food service systems, including human resource, financial, and facility management. Distribution and service. Equipment and layout in food service facilities. Completion of facility planning project.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 3680 or FN 358, and NTR 3680L or FN 358L.

courses.title: Health Science and Nutrition Graduate Program Exploration and Preparation
courses.description: Exploration of post- baccalaureate programs for health science and nutrition programs, including option exploration includes school search, program evaluation, application process and includes identifying appropriate programs and internships, completing the application, developing resumes and portfolio components, and improving interviewing skills.
courses.prerequisites: Nutrition major and senior standing. FST majors and other College of Agriculture majors will be considered per instructor approval.

courses.title: Space Nutrition
courses.description: The effects of long-term space travel on the human body, such as changes to nutrient requirements, muscle atrophy, bone loss, and oxidative stress. Nutrition and exercise recommendations will be covered that will help to offset these encountered challenges.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 2030 , NTR 2350 , or NTR 3050 .

courses.title: Nutritional Genomics
courses.description: Nutritional genomics examines the integral role of dietary bioactive components in the regulation of gene expression on phenotype, assessing the effects of genetic variations and polymorphisms, characterizing gene networks that affect cellular metabolism, and delays the onset of chronic disease. Students should have a basic understanding of biochemistry, nutrition, and metabolism. Knowledge of basic genetics or molecular biology preferred, but not required.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 3930 , FN 433, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Internship in Food and Nutrition
courses.description: On-the-job training in foods and nutrition, providing professional level experiences in food service, community nutrition, research, and quality control. Experiences may be useful for preparation of senior projects.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent.

courses.title: Internship in Food and Nutrition
courses.description: On-the-job training in foods and nutrition, providing professional level experiences in food service, community nutrition, research, and quality control. Experiences may be useful for preparation of senior projects.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent.

courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy I
courses.description: Pathophysiology of selected medical problems with specific attention to nutritional needs and treatment as part of evidenced based practice nutritional care. Clinical nutrition applications in acute and chronic diseases. Nutritional care process, medical terminology, charting and documentation, and case study discussions. Corequisite(s): NTR 4430L .
courses.prerequisites: C or better in NTR 3930 or FN 434.

courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy Laboratory
courses.description: Pathophysiology of selected medical problems with specific attention to nutritional needs and treatment as part of evidenced based practice and nutritional/medical care. Clinical nutrition applications in acute and chronic disease. Nutritional care process, medical terminology, charting and documentation, patient simulations and healthcare laboratory experiments, and case studies. 1 three-hour laboratory. Corequisite(s): NTR 4430 .
courses.prerequisites: C or better in NTR 3930 .

courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II
courses.description: Dual Listed as: NTR 5240 Continuation of Medical Nutrition Therapy I. Pathophysiology of selected medical problems with specific attention to nutritional needs and treatment as part of evidenced-based practice and nutritional/medical care. Clinical nutrition applications in acute and chronic disease. Nutritional care process, medical terminology, charting and documentation, and case study discussions. Capstone for senior Dietetics students. Corequisite(s): May be taken concurrently with NTR 5250 with consent of the instructor.
courses.prerequisites: Senior or graduate standing, and a C or better in NTR 4430 and NTR 4430L . A background or experience in biochemistry, nutrition, and metabolism is recommended.

courses.title: Medical Nutrition Counseling for the Hispanic/Latino Population Activity
courses.description: Spanish medical nutrition therapy terminology and pathophysiology of chronic diseases. Reviews theory and practice of nutrition counseling by emphasizing development of active listening, questioning and reflection. Involves role playing, presentation of case studies and behavior modification.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 3280A and NTR 3350A . Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 4440 .

courses.title: Community Nutrition
courses.description: Goals and trends in community nutrition. Dietary methodology. National nutrition status surveys. Role of public and private agencies in community nutrition programs. Analytical tools. Grantsmanship, public policy and legislation. Corequisite(s): NTR 4460A or NTR 4460AS.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in NTR 3450 or FN 345, NTR 3450A or FN 345L, and NTR 4430 or FN 443.

courses.title: Community Nutrition Activity
courses.description: Goals and trends in community nutrition. Dietary methodology. National nutrition status surveys. Role of public and private agencies in community nutrition programs. Analytical tools. Grantsmanship, public policy and legislation. Corequisite(s): NTR 4460 or NTR 4460S .
courses.prerequisites: C or better in NTR 3450 or FN 345, NTR 3450A or FN 345L, and NTR 4430 or FN 443.

courses.title: Nutrition for Sport and Exercise
courses.description: An in-depth discussion on the integration of nutrition, physiology, exercise, and dietary supplements for optimizing sports performance and body composition. It also prioritizes the application of current research findings in regards to nutrition, athletic performance, and body weight changes.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in NTR 2350 , FN 235, NTR 3050 , or FN 305.

courses.title: Nutrition Research Methods
courses.description: Introduction to research in nutrition as the foundation for evidence-based practice. The scientific method, hypothesis testing, clinical trials, epidemiological research, nutrition surveys, and sensory analysis. Weekly writing assignments. Reading and critiquing research papers.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and Instructor consent.

courses.title: Statistics for Nutrition and Dietetics
courses.description: Introduction to statistical procedures as applied to nutrition. Statistical software such as SPSS and NVivo will be used to analyze data. Application of both parametric and nonparametric statistical tests. A focus on statistical approaches for community nutrition and public health will be emphasized.
courses.prerequisites: STA 1201 or equivalent, and completion of accredited Baccalaureate degree requirements as specified by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics; or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Critical Evaluation of Nutrition Practice and Research
courses.description: Introduction to research in nutrition as the foundation for evidence-based practice such as: scientific method, hypothesis testing, clinical trials, epidemiologicalresearch, nutrition surveys, and dietary analysis. Explore current nutritional recommendations and topical areas of nutrition. Weekly writing assignments. Reading and critiquing research papers.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; and grade of B or better in NTR 2350 and STA 1200 .

courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II
courses.description: Dual Listed as: NTR 4440 Continuation of Medical Nutrition Therapy I. Pathophysiology of selected medical problems with specific attention to nutritional needs and treatment as part of evidenced-based practice and nutritional/medical care. Clinical nutrition applications in acute and chronic disease. Nutritional care process, medical terminology, charting and documentation, and case study discussions. Capstone for senior Dietetics students. Corequisite(s): May be taken concurrently with NTR 5250 with instructor consent.
courses.prerequisites: Senior or graduate standing, and a C or better in NTR 4430 and NTR 4430L . A background or experience in biochemistry, nutrition, and metabolism is recommended.

courses.title: A Life Course Approach to Nutrition Disease Prevention, and Treatment
courses.description: Discuss developmental physiology and cellular growth and differentiation from pre-conception to old age interact with the etiology and prevention of disease. Focus on a life-course approach to life-long influences on the development of disease and evidence-based treatment. Pathophysiology of selected medical problems throughout the lifecycle with specific attention to nutrition needs and treatment as part of evidence-based practice. Advanced clinical nutrition applications in acute and chronic diseases and review of the nutritionally relevant chronic diseases with aging. Oral presentation and discussion of the scientific literature related to the life cycle. Acute and chronic disease conditions throughout the lifecycle will be explored through lectures, case discussions, assigned readings, programmed learning guides, and class presentations. Topics include, but are not limited to: critical thinking, pediatric nutrition, clinical basis of disease processes, and medical, surgical, and diet therapies for acute and chronic disease in adults and pediatrics, enteral and parenteral nutrition, malnutrition and high-risk conditions including cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal and liver disease, critical care, HIV/AIDS, and oncology. Corequisite(s): Admission into the MS in Applied Nutrition program.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 4440 , NTR 5240 , or consent of instructor. A background or experience in biochemistry, nutrition, and metabolism is recommended.

courses.title: Food Science and Safety Online
courses.description: Explore regulations involving food safety, sanitation, handling, processing, distribution, import and export, ingredients, misbranding, and nutrition labeling. Student-led discussions, case studies, and project concerning current issues in food industries and the governmental laws and regulations related to those issues.
courses.prerequisites: Current ServSafe certification and completion of accredited Baccalaureate degree requirements as specified by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics; or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Nutrition- Experimental Basis of the Dietary Recommended Intakes
courses.description: Study of the experimental basis for determination of the Dietary Recommended Intakes (DRIs). Evaluation of the interrelationships between metabolism, physiology, and genetics with nutrient requirements. The role of the DRIs in preventing nutritional inadequacy and prevention of chronic disease will be examined. Written exams and oral presentations. 2 hours lectures/problem-solving.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 3930 or instructor consent.

courses.title: Recent Advances in Nutrient Metabolism I, II
courses.description: Recent developments and research in nutrient metabolism. A major nutrient class (proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals) will be studied during each semester. Each course to be subtitled identifying the nutrient class to be discussed. May be taken up to two times, only with different topics, for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 5330 , or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Advanced Life Cycle Nutrition
courses.description: Discussion of how developmental physiology and cellular growth and differentiation influence nutrient requirements during pregnancy and lactation, fetal growth, infancy, premature birth, childhood, adolescence adulthood and old age. Planning nutrition programs to meet the nutrient needs of at-risk women, infants and children. Review of the nutritionally relevant chronic diseases with aging. Oral presentation and discussion of the scientific literature related to the life cycle.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 3930 , FN 434, or instructor consent; NTR 3940 , FN 435, or instructor consent; and Dietetic Internship Eligible (DPD director consent).

courses.title: Advanced Medical Nutrition Therapy
courses.description: Pathophysiology of selected medical problems with specific attention to nutritional needs and treatment as part of evidenced based practice medical care. Advanced clinical nutrition applications in acute and chronic diseases. Nutritional care process, medical terminology, charting and documentation, and case study discussions. Corequisite(s): NTR 5450 and NTR 5600 .
courses.prerequisites: Bachelor’s degree approved by Commission on Accreditation for Dietetic Educ; and accepted into CPP Dietetic Internship Program.

courses.title: Advanced Medical Nutrition II
courses.description: Application of critical thinking skills and integrate the theories and principles of Medical nutrition therapy (MNT) into clinical practice. Case studies and an evidence-based approach to practice will be used to integrate and utilize their knowledge of nutrition, metabolism, and physiology, for effectively planning and managing the nutritional care of patients using the Nutrition Care Process. Acute and chronic disease conditions will be explored through lectures, case discussions, assigned readings, programmed learning guides, and class presentations. Topics include: critical thinking, pediatric nutrition, clinical basis of disease processes, and medical, surgical, and diet therapies for acute and chronic disease in adults and pediatrics, enteral and parenteral nutrition, malnutrition and high risk conditions including cardiovascular, pulmonary, renal and liver disease, critical care, HIV/AIDS, and oncology.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 5430 and completion of accredited Baccalaureate degree requirements as specified by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics; or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Nutrition Education and Counseling
courses.description: Examination of the theoretical perspectives on nutrition, food and health-related behavior change. Study of the key constructs from a variety of nutrition and health behavior theories and frameworks such as the Theory of Planned Behavior, the Health Belief Model, Social Cognitive Theory and the Trans-Theoretical Model. Effective teaching strategies and procedural models for designing effective nutrition education programs targeting the general public will be presented to enable students to design and deliver interventions and programs in the community and clinical settings
courses.prerequisites: Completion of accredited Baccalaureate degree requirements as specified by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics, or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Current Topics in Clinical Practice I, II
courses.description: Presentations by professionals on selected topics. Student presentations of case studies and position papers. Professional portfolio creation. Critiques of peer-reviewed articles. 150 hours of experiential practice. Must enroll in the NTR 5450 course for two consecutive semesters while completing the Master of Science in Agriculture - Nutrition and Food Science Option. Corequisite(s): NTR 5600 and NTR 5610 .
courses.prerequisites: Admission into the MS in Agriculture - Nutrition and Food Science Option.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units, with a maximum of 2 units per semester.

courses.title: Obesity and Chronic Disease
courses.description: Introduction to the multifactorial aspects of obesity, maintenance of a healthy weight, the relationship of weight status to chronic disease prevention, and provide an overview of obesity/overweight, chronic disease, and their relationship to public health practice. Traditional and novel nutrition and behavior theories will also be discussed. A rigorous, evidence-based exploration of the issue of obesity. Through process-oriented assignments and discussions students formulate their own perspectives on origins, prevention, and treatment of obesity and its relationship to chronic disease.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 5360 or equivalent, and completion of accredited Baccalaureate degree requirements as specified by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics; or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Clinical Practice I
courses.description: Supervised pre-professional practice and on-the-job training in nutrition and dietetics. This internship course is a high-impact practice (HIP) to enhance the knowledge and application of skills of the MS in Nutrition students. Gain hands-on experience working with nutrition and dietetic companies that serve the needs of the nutrition market. An opportunity to network with the industry for future jobs. The experience must be new to the student. Students must obtain instructor/advisor/preceptor approval of the Internship experience. Periodic analysis of internship experience is reported in written journal reflections. *Students in the DI track option will take this course for 4 credits, as it serves as their ACEND required supervised practice. Non-DI track option will take this course for 2 credits. *For students enrolled in the Dietetics track option: Supervised pre-professional practice in assigned clinical, community and food service sites, minimum of 350-500 hours. *For students enrolled in the non-Dietetics track option: Supervised pre-professional practice in an internship experience identified by the student and their advisor/instructor. Corequisite(s): NTR 5450 - Current Topics in Clinical Practice I, II (2) NTR 5450 (Dietetics subplan/track/option only)*.
courses.prerequisites: Bachelor’s degree; and verification statement approved by Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND), accepted in the MS in Applied Nutrition (Blended), or accepted into CPP Dietetic Internship Program.

courses.title: Clinical Practice II
courses.description: Supervised pre-professional practice and on-the-job training in nutrition and dietetics. This internship class is a high-impact practice (HIP) to enhance the knowledge and application of skills of the MS in Applied Nutrition students. Students will get hands-on experience working with nutrition and dietetic companies that serve the needs of the nutrition market. An opportunity to network with the industry for future jobs. The experience must be new to the student. Students must obtain instructor/advisor/preceptor approval of the Internship experience. Periodic analysis of internship experience is reported in written journal reflections. Students in Dietetics Internship will take this course for 4 credits, as it serves as their ACEND required supervised practice. Non-Dietetics Internship students will take this course for 2 credits. For students enrolled in DI: Supervised pre-professional practice in assigned clinical, community and food service sites, minimum of 350-500 hours. For students enrolled in non-DI: Supervised pre-professional practice in an internship experience identified by the student and their advisor/instructor. Corequisite(s): NTR 5450 (Dietetics Internship students only).
courses.prerequisites: Bachelor’s degree; and verification statement approved by Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND), accepted in the MS in Applied Nutrition, or accepted into CPP Dietetic Internship Program.

courses.title: Integrated Nutrition and Functional Medicine
courses.description: An introduction to integrative and complimentary nutrition for health and wellness. Reviews the most commonly used complementary and alternative medicine modalities centered on the five domains of Complementary, Integrative, and Alternative Medicine: Alternative Medical Systems, Mind-Body Medicine, Manual Therapies, Energy-Based Therapies, and Biologically-based Therapies. Presentation on the theory and principles of Complementary and Alternative Medicine practices and will critically evaluate evidence of their efficacy and safety.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 5430 or equivalent, and completion of accredited Baccalaureate degree requirements as specified by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics; or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Seminar in Nutrition
courses.description: Study of selected topic in nutrition or food science. Each seminar subtitled to describe its emphasis. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 5100 or instructor consent.

courses.title: Seminar in Nutrition-Journal Club
courses.description: Study of selected topics in nutrition or food science in a Journal Club format. Each seminar is subtitled to describe its emphasis. Total credit limited to 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 5100 or instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units.

courses.title: Leadership and Entrepreneurship in Nutrition
courses.description: Explore the qualifications of leadership and entrepreneurship within the field of Nutrition. Will involve case study reviews and practical application to prepare students for leadership positions and possible development of nutrition-related businesses. Corequisite(s): Admission into the MS in Applied Nutrition program.

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing and Instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students Activity
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course. Corequisite(s): NTR 5990 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing and Instructor Consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students Laboratory
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course. Corequisite(s): NTR 5990 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing and Instructor Consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Advanced Nutrition Lifecycle II (Pediatrics)
courses.description: Examination of the physiological, biochemical, and nutritional aspects of disease processes throughout the lifecycle, with a focus on infants and children up to 18 years of age. Nutrition needs throughout stages of the life cycle, including pregnancy and lactation, infancy, adolescence, and aging; and the socioeconomic, cultural, and psychological influences on food and nutrition behavior. Medical Nutrition Therapy for a variety of medical conditions found in this population will be discussed, including: inborn errors of metabolism, food hypersensitivity, obesity, and diseases of the major organ systems.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 5360 , NTR 5440 , and completion of accredited Baccalaureate degree requirements as specified by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics; or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Nutrition and Food Management
courses.description: The organization and administration of foodservice and nutrition systems and the functions and responsibilities specific to management; decision-making, planning, organizing, and staffing. Examination of the complex responsibilities of the nutrition and dietetics professional in food management, including the essentials of operating a foodservice facility - menu planning, purchasing, storage, issuing, food production, service, distribution, quality control, and food safety.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 3680 , NTR 5325 , and completion of accredited Baccalaureate degree requirements as specified by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics; or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Community Nutrition
courses.description: Explore skills needed and their application in community and public health settings. Evaluate the barriers to disease prevention and health promotion, factors that influence personal health decisions, preventive interventions directed at individuals (clinical settings) and populations (community settings), strategies for using population health principles. Familiarization with community-based research and programs focused on nutrition or has nutrition as a component such as community non-profit agencies, worksites, health centers, clinics, hospitals, schools, churches, supermarkets, recreational and sports centers, and councils on aging/senior centers, and food assistant programs.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 5446 or equivalent, and completion of accredited Baccalaureate degree requirements as specified by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics; or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Qualitative Research II
courses.description: Provides the opportunity for students to implement and apply Qualitative Research methodologies including triangulation interviews (assessment), and conducting, transcribing and analyzing information from a focus group (study implementation). Presentations and peer reviews will contribute to the evaluation component of their activities. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 6594 .

courses.title: Nutrition in Sports and Exercise
courses.description: Knowledge concerning the role of nutrients in optimizing human performance. Assessment of caloric and nutrient requirements associate with exercise. Special considerations is given to gender specific needs of athletes, nutritional ergogenic aids, and eating disorders.
courses.prerequisites: NTR 3930 or FN 434. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 5100 .

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Individual study/investigation and research in a specialized area proposed by the student with the approval, and under the supervision, of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Proposal Defense Presentation
courses.description: A public oral presentation and discussion of a written proposed research plan for the master’s thesis. Required for Advancement to Candidacy. Unconditional standing required. Required for Advancement to Candidacy. Required for Advancement to Candidacy. Corequisite(s): AG 5300 .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Advisor consent.

courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Individual research in an area of specialization conducted as part of the preparation for writing a thesis under the direction of graduate faculty.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 6930 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Maximum of 4 units.

courses.title: Capstone Project - Preparation
courses.description: In coordination with faculty and/or internship sites, students will use their experiences to identify an issue of concern or improvement project on which to focus for their independent research. Design and develop a terminal project that demonstrates the skills and knowledge achieved in the graduate program.

courses.title: Capstone Project - Presentation
courses.description: In coordination with faculty and/or internship sites, conduct independent research leading to the design, development and completion of a terminal project that demonstrates the skills and knowledge achieved in the graduate program.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of all courses during year one of program including successful completion of NTR 6945 and overall GPA of 3.0 or higher in graduate courses.

courses.title: Master’s Thesis Defense
courses.description: Compilation of data culminating in the summarizing and reporting, in thesis form, of independent supervised research. Advancement to Candidacy required ( NTR 6930 ).
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and Instructor consent. Pre or Corequisite(s): NTR 6940 .

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and Instructor consent.
